name: Statistician
title: Statistician (Indian Statistical Service)
intro: From Class 12 with Maths to the Indian Statistical Service or a data career: B.Sc Statistics, an optional M.Sc, the UPSC IES/ISS exam, then ISS officer or industry analytics.

phases.title: Class 12 with Maths
phases.summary: Maths is what matters; Commerce and Arts students with Maths can join too.
points: Build a strong maths foundation in Class 11–12.
Many universities admit Commerce and Arts students with Maths to B.Sc/BA Statistics.
Science students are eligible by default.

phases.title: B.Sc Statistics
points: For ISS, Statistics, Mathematical Statistics or Applied Statistics must be one of the subjects in your bachelor's.
A BA Economics counts only if Statistics was one of the subjects.
Learn R, Python or SQL — private roles ask for them.

phases.title: M.Sc Statistics (optional)
points: A master's in Statistics, Mathematical Statistics or Applied Statistics also makes you eligible for ISS.
It helps for UPSC preparation and research.
The Indian Statistical Institute and universities run statistics research.

phases.title: UPSC IES/ISS exam
phases.summary: General English, General Studies and statistics papers, then an interview.
points: UPSC conducts one combined examination for the Indian Economic Service and Indian Statistical Service, with different papers for each.
ISS papers: General English, General Studies and statistics papers, followed by an interview.
Age limits and relaxations are in the current UPSC notice; other routes are SSC CGL statistical posts and state statistical services.

phases.title: ISS officer or analyst
points: ISS entry: Group A central services start at Level 10 of the 7th CPC pay matrix (₹56,100 entry basic), plus DA, HRA and other allowances.
Government: MoSPI, NSO, ministries, RBI and statistical bodies; senior ISS officers serve across MoSPI and ministries.
Private: analytics firms, pharma (clinical trials), insurance, banks and market research.
